next_step: Closed-lost. Re-engage in 6 months after model quality fixes and security PT report.
notes:
Summary: Closed-lost (customer selected incumbent). Primary reason: model quality regression on our POC vs their incumbent (structured JSON outputs and tool-calls to EHR connectors were brittle).

Key background:
- Cartwheel builds clinical automation for discharge summaries, med reconciliation, and payer-facing docs. Heavy downstream consumers expect exact JSON schema; small format deviations break ingestion.
- Security & residency critical: must run in VPC/on-prem with KMS + audit logging.

Timeline / recent activity (shorthand):
- 2024-09-12: inbound MQL -> intro call (AE Sofia). ff-2024-09-12-intro.
- 2024-09-25: scoping call w/ Eng + Security (Ethan SE joined). noted need for deterministic function-calling to EHR. ff-2024-09-25-scope.
- 2024-10-03: POC kicked off (3-week). baseline tests supplied (2000 clinical notes; strict JSON schema). ff-2024-10-03-cartwheel-intro.
- 2024-11-04: POC interim review — observed token-level quality issues: hallucinated fields, inconsistent date formats, missing required keys. Filed ticket CART-1259.
- 2024-11-07: POC final run vs incumbent. Customer test harness showed incumbent (OpenAI) median schema pass-rate 98% vs Redwood 83%. ff-2024-11-07-poc-review. Link: drive:/deals/cartwheel/cartwheel-redwood-poc-results-2024-11.pdf
- 2024-11-15: Security questionnaire submitted (large list). SEC-3421 created for pen-test scope. drive:/security/cartwheel/security-questions-redwood-2025-01.xlsx.
- 2024-12-02: Competitor demo recap — Cartwheel procurement says incumbent promised guaranteed pass-rates and integration support.
- 2025-01-21: Security debrief — Cartwheel awaiting Redwood PT report; procurement under hiring freeze; finance delaying sign. ff-2025-01-21-security-debrief.
- 2025-02-14: Final decision call — closed-lost to incumbent. Reasons: quality delta on structured output; incumbent offered contract language on remediation SLA; procurement freeze/finance conservative. thread_abc123_cartwheel_poc referenced.

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "We can't risk breaking downstream ingestion — we need deterministic JSON and reliable function-calls to our EHR."
- "The incumbent matched our schema 99% of the time; your model was promising but regressions in edge cases are deal-breakers."

POC technical notes (from SE):
- Failures concentrated on: lists of medications (ordering and dosage fields), date/time normalization (ISO vs localized), and function-call retries when connector returned 5xx.
- Root cause hypothesis: Redwood quantized model variant used for cost/test run lost fidelity on structured token sequences; minibatching introduced non-determinism in tool-calling order.
- Proposed mitigations discussed: pinning higher-precision model variant, deterministic function-calling wrapper, stricter post-processing validation (schema linter).

Why stalled / closed-lost:
- Quality regression vs incumbent on critical integration flows -> technical risk perceived too high.
- No internal champion after lead eng moved teams (no_champion).
- Procurement/hiring freeze slowed contracting and removed urgency.
- Security requested company-wide pen-test results; Redwood's PT timeline > Cartwheel's procurement window.

Next steps / playbook suggestions (internal):
- Mark as closed-lost with reason tags: quality_regression, security_timing, no_champion.
- Capture POC artifacts and run targeted follow-up: re-run POC with pinned non-quantized model + deterministic function-calling shim, produce a 3rd-party schema pass-rate report.
- When PT report ready and model patch applied, request win-back conversation in 6 months.
- Consider offering a time-bound remediation SLA and integration engineering hours to mitigate incumbent advantage.

Attachments / refs: CART-1259 (POC failures), SEC-3421 (security PT scope), drive:/deals/cartwheel/cartwheel-redwood-poc-results-2024-11.pdf, ff-2024-11-07-poc-review.

Notes added by: Sofia Ramirez (AE) + Ethan Cole (SE) on 2025-02-28.
